quiz.q: In Karl Mannheim's sociology of knowledge, how do 'ideology' and 'utopia' differ?
options: Ideology preserves dominant class power, whereas utopia reflects exploited class visions seeking transformation.
Ideology represents objective scientific knowledge, whereas utopia represents distorted false consciousness.
Ideology serves as a totalitarian instrument of terror, whereas utopia represents open society values.
Ideology organizes exploited classes for revolution, whereas utopia justifies the status quo of ruling elites.
quiz.why: Mannheim distinguished ideology as ideas defending dominant class interests from utopia as aspirations of the exploited seeking change.

quiz.q: How does Francis Fukuyama's 'End of History' thesis differ from Daniel Bell's 'End of Ideology' thesis?
options: It rejects Western capitalism in favor of technocratic, non-ideological state welfare administration.
It assertively crowns liberalism as humanity's final ideological endpoint, rather than declaring ideological struggles meaningless.
It argues that all societies inevitably pass through identical, non-ideological stages of economic growth.
It claims ideological conflict has ceased because bureaucratic management completely replaced political decision-making.
quiz.why: Unlike the End of Ideology which viewed ideological conflict as obsolete, Fukuyama assertively claimed liberalism represents humanity's final ideological destination.

quiz.q: According to Thomas Kuhn's theory of paradigms, why does science lack absolute finality?
options: Scientific inquiry is purely subjective perception driven exclusively by individual wills to power.
Scientific knowledge accumulates linearly without ever encountering fundamental crises or conceptual shifts.
Scientists operate within temporary conceptual frameworks that are replaced when unanswered questions trigger crisis.
Science functions merely as an instrument of state terror designed to enforce totalitarian control.
quiz.why: Kuhn showed that scientists work within paradigms that face crisis when anomalies accumulate, leading to replacement by new paradigms.

quiz.q: Why do postmodern thinkers like Jean-François Lyotard reject modernist meta-narratives?
options: They argue meta-narratives lack sufficient empirical scientific verification to establish objective foundational truths.
They believe universal frameworks lead to political anarchy and prevent the formation of radical democracies.
They maintain that grand theories cannot explain human society without relying on colonial anthropological binaries.
They contend totalising theories falsely claim universal truth while suppressing diverse, local perspectives.
quiz.why: Lyotard defined postmodernism as incredulity toward meta-narratives because universal theories impose totalising explanations that erase diverse, local truths.
